interface.name: xfce_output_manager_private_v1
interface.description:
This protocol advertises extensions to the existing wl_output and xdg_output_v1 protocols.
It is intended to be private to the Xfce desktop implementation, and should not be used by other applications. This protocol may introduce incompatible changes at any time, without warning, and without following normal, accepted guidelines about Wayland protocol versioning.
This protocol depends on the wl_output protocol (with a soft dependency on the xdg_output_v1 protocol).

request.name: get_xfce_output
request.description: This creates a new xfce_output_v1 object for the given wl_output.

arg.name: output
arg.summary: Output to request a xfce_output_v1 object for

description.summary: Informs the compositor the client is done using the manager object

event.name: serial

description.summary: Advertises the serial number of a device

event.description:
This informs the client of the output's hardware serial number.
This event is emitted on creation of the xfce_output_v1 instance, if the serial number is available.
Since the serial number will never change during the lifetime of this output object, it is safe to assume you will only get this event once for each xfce_output_v1.
This event is a property that is a part of the 'done' grouping. See the xfce_output_v1.done event for more information.

event.name: edid

description.summary: Advertises the EDID of a device

event.description:
The EDID data is raw binary data exposed by the monitor's hardware and will need to be parsed in order to be useful.
This event is emitted on creation of the xfce_output_v1 instance, if the EDID is available.
Since the EDID will never change during the lifetime of this output object, it is safe to assume you will only get this event once for each xfce_output_v1.
This event is a property that is a part of the 'done' grouping. See the xfce_output_v1.done event for more information.

arg.name: fd
arg.summary: A file descriptor that can be mapped into memory

arg.name: size
arg.summary: The size of the memory region referred to by fd

event.name: primary

description.summary: Emitted when the output becomes primary

event.description:
The user or compositor may have designated an output as "primary", which is the output that might usually hold the desktop's main UI elements, like a panel or dock.
Since only one output can be primary, receiving this event means that the previous primary output is no longer primary.
This event is a property that is a part of the 'done' grouping. See the xfce_output_v1.done event for more information.

event.name: workarea

description.summary: Advertises the usable space on the output

event.description:
An output's workarea is the area that is usable for the display of regular surfaces. For example, a panel or dock may reserve space at the edge of the screen where other surfaces should not be placed, so the area taken up by the panel or dock would be excluded by the workkarea.
Coordinates and size are presented in output-relative, logical coordinates that may be scaled (see xdg_output_v1.logical_size for details), with the (0, 0) origin in the top-left corner.
The workarea event will always be emitted after binding the object, even if the coordinates and size represent the full output area. It will be emitted again any time the workarea changes.
This event is a property that is a part of the 'done' grouping. See the xfce_output_v1.done event for more information.

event.name: done
event.description:
Sent after a grouping of event properties has been sent.
After initially creating the object, all known properties will be sent before this event is sent. When properties change, their events will be succeeded by this event.
See the individual events to learn which events are part of the initial 'done' group.

event.name: pointer_enter

description.summary: Emitted when a pointer enters this output

event.description:
The pointer for a seat can only be on one output at a time, so, aside from the first emission of this event, it will never be emitted without being preceded by a pointer_leave event from another xfce_output_v1 instance.
This event will be emitted at bind time to inform new clients of the output the pointer is currently on.
Note that this event is _not_ part of the 'done' group.

event.name: pointer_leave

description.summary: Emitted when a pointer leaves this output

event.description:
The pointer for a seat can only be on one output at a time, so this event will never be emitted without being preceded by a pointer_enter event on the same object.
Note that this event is _not_ part of the 'done' group.
